A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same parameter-specialization study. Their text, equations, six figures, five tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 20 language models on SpecWiki, controlled finetuning experiments, and supplementary dataset-validation and popularity-frequency results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 4–5 and Appendices A–B, including model comparisons, finetuning outcomes, and dataset-validation analyses.

M1.justification: The activation-based vector selection, masking procedure, and four finetuning strategies in Sections 3 and 5 are unchanged. The added mixture-of-experts and sparse-autoencoder discussion proposes future extensions, without introducing an implemented component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 525-concept SpecWiki multiple-choice and open-ended tasks, supplementary finetuning data for ten high-frequency concepts, and The Pile frequency analysis. No new domain or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same untuned LLaMA2-7B and Qwen2-7B models and FT-FV, FT-CV, and FT-RV comparators to FT-PV. The model comparison sets elsewhere also match; the newly cited architectures are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Both retain ten concept-related and fifty irrelevant questions, masking proportions of 10%–50%, exclusion of the first five layers, and three-shot MCQ versus zero-shot open-ended evaluation. The finetuning and supplementary-analysis protocols are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The masking-rate, model-scale, pretraining-checkpoint, concept-popularity, and finetuning-control analyses are retained unchanged. Appendix manual verification and popularity-frequency validation are relocated or renumbered, without added analyses.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same ± reporting, and Figures 2 and 6 retain their correlation statistics and p-values. V2 adds no run counts, seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results, and reported findings match. For example, Table 2 retains FT-PV MCQ/OEG accuracies of 0.67/0.59 for LLaMA2-7B and 0.77/0.70 for Qwen2-7B; the appendix popularity-frequency correlation remains 0.814.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, including the masking formulation and Parameter Specialization Score definition, are unchanged. The hallucination-metric formulas move from Appendix C.3 to B.3 without mathematical revisions; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about quantifying specialization, its association with stronger models, and the benefits of targeted finetuning. The added future directions do not redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds a conceptual connection to expert-parameter specialization in mixture-of-experts models and reduced feature superposition in sparse autoencoders, motivating future extensions. The MLP-only analysis and model-size limitations already appeared in v1 Appendix A and are merely relocated.

D1.justification: Dataset prompts, inference instructions, token limits, and the four 80GB NVIDIA A800 GPU disclosure are unchanged. Renumbering the dataset and experiment appendices introduces no additional implementation, hyperparameter, or code/data-access information.

R1.justification: V2 adds Fedus et al. (2022) on Switch Transformers and Huben et al. (2024) on sparse autoencoders, connecting their specialization and superposition mechanisms to future research. Existing references and the main related-work positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Limitations and Future Work moves from Appendix A to Section 7, with a short extension and corresponding appendix renumbering. V2 also adds a funding acknowledgment and updates affiliation, contact, and conference information; the main scientific narrative is unchanged.

P2.justification: All six figures and five tables retain their content and captions. Figure 6 moves from the standalone final page to appendix page 18, while the title page, references, and appendix text reflow; no scientific display is added or redrawn.

improvement.justification: Moving the existing scope limitations into Section 7 makes them more prominent, and the specific connections to mixture-of-experts and sparse-autoencoder research modestly improve contextualization. These are limited organizational and explanatory benefits: the methods, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
